Email Phone Send Course Outline for AZ-900 Exam/ Az-900: Syllabus and Format The AZ-900 test syllabus places a strong emphasis on core concepts of cloud-based services in respect to Azure. Core Azure services, including storage, computing, and networking, are included. The Azure support model, and security and pricing, privacy services are also included. Usually, there are 40–60 questions with a large number of multiple-choice responses. This exam can be completed in an hour. The following table breaks down the proportion of the module’s competencies that must be acquired to pass the test: Describe cloud concepts (15-20%) Understanding the variations among public, private, and hybrid cloud models. When on-premises infrastructure or a private cloud are combined with a public cloud, a hybrid cloud results, allowing data and apps to travel back and forth between the two. Virtual machines are just one type of cloud service; there are also platform-as-a-service (PaaS), infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), software-as-a-service (SaaS), and serverless services. Knowing the advantages of adopting Azure and the differences between capital expenditure (CapEx) and operational expenditure (OpEx), as well as terminologies like agility, availability, scalability, fault tolerance, and disaster recovery Describe Core Azure Services – 15-20% You will learn about the fundamental Microsoft Azure architectural elements in this domain. Resource Groups, Regions and Region Pairs, Availability Zones, Management Groups, Subscriptions and Resource Managers are all added in terms of their advantages and ways to use them. In addition, you should be familiar with the functions and advantages of app services, virtual machines (VMs), Azure Container Instances (ACI), virtual desktops, and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). This domain also encompasses ExpressRoute, Disc Storage, Container Storage, File Storage, VPN Gateways, Virtual Networks, Virtual Network Peering, and Virtual Networks. Cosmos DB, Azure Database for MySQL Azure SQL Database, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and SQL Managed Instance are also comprised. Storage levels are also included. To become a Pro in Azure Cloud Computing check Azure Training in pune . Describe the Core Management Tools and Azure Solutions – 10-15% This class covers the essential inquiries relating to the core Azure solutions. IoT Central, IoT (Internet of Things) Hub, Azure Sphere, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Databricks, and HDInsight usage and advantages should be familiar to you. Furthermore, you should be prepared for inquiries and issues pertaining to Azure management tools, including Azure Portal, Azure PowerShell, Azure CLI, Cloud Shell and Azure Mobile App,. Explaining how to use ARM (Azure Resource Manager templates, Azure Monitor, Azure Service Health, and Azure Advisor) should come after preparation. Explain Network Security and General Security Features – 10-15% In this area, Microsoft Azure’s security tools like the Azure Security Centre are taken into account. It covers resource hygiene, policy compliance, security alerts, and secure score. Additionally, it includes Key Vault, Dedicated Hosts, and Azure Sentinel. You will also gain knowledge of network security fields such as functional ideas, NSG (Network Security Groups) defense and usage, Azure DDoS protection, and firewall protection. Explain the governance, identity, compliance, and privacy features (20-25%). In this category, you will study topics like Azure Identity Services. Conditional Access,Azure Active Directory, SSO (Single Sign-On) and MFA (multi-factor authentication are given a lot of attention. There are also inquiries about Azure Governance features. You should explain how Azure Blueprints, RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), Cloud Adoption Framework, resource locks and tags are used and function. The utilization of Microsoft’s Privacy Statement, OST (Online Service Terms), DPA (Data Protection Amendment), Azure Sovereign Regions, Azure compliance paperwork and Trust Centre are all examples of compliance and privacy resources that you should be able to articulate. Explain Azure’s service level agreements and cost management (between 10% and 15%). The final item on this list focuses on various methods of cost management and planning. You must be able to recognize the various elements influencing expenses as well as those contributing to cost savings. You should also be able to describe the operation and application of a pricing calculator and TCO. ACM (Azure Cost Management) usage and functionality should also be described. In particular, service life cycles and Azure SLAs are given special consideration in this domain. How to Register for AZ-900 Exam: Registering for the AZ-900 exam is a straightforward process facilitated through the official Microsoft Learn website. Prospective candidates can initiate the registration by navigating to the dedicated AZ-900 exam page, where they will discover comprehensive instructions to guide them seamlessly through the registration procedure. A prerequisite for registration is a Microsoft account, easily created if not already possessed. The exam registration provides candidates with the flexibility to choose between two options: selecting an on-site test center or opting for the convenience of an online proctored exam. This choice caters to individual preferences and ensures accessibility for candidates worldwide. Critical steps in the registration process include a thorough review of exam details, confirmation of eligibility, and the completion of the payment process. Emphasizing the importance of adequate preparation, candidates are encouraged to utilize the available study resources and practice exams before scheduling the AZ-900 exam. This proactive approach contributes to a more confident and successful exam experience, aligning with Microsoft’s commitment to providing a streamlined and accessible certification process for individuals seeking proficiency in Microsoft Azure fundamentals. Exam Retake Policy: Microsoft’s AZ-900 exam retake policy is designed with fairness and flexibility, recognizing the diverse learning curves of candidates. In the event of not passing the exam on the initial attempt, individuals are granted the opportunity for a swift retake after a minimal waiting period of at least 24 hours. This immediate reattempt allows candidates to capitalize on their recent exam experience, quickly address any identified weaknesses, and fortify their understanding for a more successful outcome. For subsequent retakes, a 14-day waiting period is imposed, maintaining a balanced approach that encourages strategic preparation and thorough review. This deliberate waiting period serves as a valuable interval for candidates to delve deeper into the exam content, address areas of improvement, and enhance their overall readiness. The retake policy, with its considerate waiting periods, not only accommodates diverse learning styles but also empowers candidates to approach the AZ-900 certification journey strategically.
